answer: Reflexion is a framework that reinforces language agents through linguistic feedback rather than by updating model weights [arxiv:2303.11366#176]. This design addresses the limitations of token-level, left-to-right generation in standard language models, which often fall short on tasks that require strategic lookahead or where initial decisions are crucial [arxiv:2305.10601#207]. answer: Self-RAG, or Self-Reflective Retrieval-Augmented Generation, is a framework that enhances the quality and factuality of large language models (LLMs) through retrieval on demand and self-reflection without sacrificing the model's original creativity and versatility [arxiv:2310.11511#606]. End-to-end training allows the model to learn to retrieve, generate, and critique its own output, leading to significant improvements in factuality [arxiv:2310.11511#619].
